This is a *comprehensive template* that demonstrates /all features/ of the ~org2html~ parser. Use this as a reference when creating your own Org-mode files for web publishing with full SEO optimization.

The template covers:
- All SEO metadata fields (title, description, Open Graph, Twitter Cards)
- Complete Org-mode syntax support
- Vue component integration via shortcodes
- Best practices for web content structure

* SEO Metadata Fields Reference                                    :seo:

** Basic Metadata

All metadata fields are defined at the top of the file using the ~#+FIELD:~ syntax:

- ~#+TITLE:~ - The main page title (appears in ~<title>~ tag and ~<h1>~)
- ~#+AUTHOR:~ - Content author name
- ~#+DATE:~ - Publication date (ISO format recommended: YYYY-MM-DD)
- ~#+EMAIL:~ - Author email address
- ~#+DESCRIPTION:~ - Meta description for search engines (150-160 characters recommended)
- ~#+KEYWORDS:~ - Comma-separated keywords for SEO
- ~#+LANGUAGE:~ - Content language code (e.g., ~en~, ~es~, ~fr~)
- ~#+CATEGORY:~ - Content category/section
- ~#+FILETAGS:~ - Org-mode tags in ~:tag1:tag2:~ format

** Advanced SEO Fields

- ~#+CANONICAL:~ - Canonical URL to prevent duplicate content issues
- ~#+COVER_IMAGE:~ - Main article image (used as fallback for social media)
- ~#+THEME_COLOR:~ - Browser theme color (hex code)
- ~#+ROBOTS:~ - Search engine directives (e.g., ~index, follow~ or ~noindex, nofollow~)

** Open Graph Metadata

Open Graph tags control how your content appears when shared on social media platforms like Facebook, LinkedIn, and Slack:

- ~#+OG_TITLE:~ - Custom title for social media (can differ from page title)
- ~#+OG_DESCRIPTION:~ - Custom description for social shares (longer than meta description)
- ~#+OG_IMAGE:~ - Social media preview image (1200x630px recommended)

If not specified, these fields fall back to ~#+TITLE:~, ~#+DESCRIPTION:~, and ~#+COVER_IMAGE:~ respectively.

** Twitter Card Metadata

Twitter Cards enhance how your content appears on Twitter/X:

- ~#+TWITTER_CARD:~ - Card type: ~summary~, ~summary_large_image~, ~app~, or ~player~
- ~#+TWITTER_SITE:~ - Your site's Twitter handle (e.g., ~@yoursite~)
- ~#+TWITTER_CREATOR:~ - Content creator's Twitter handle (e.g., ~@author~)

* Org-mode Syntax Reference                                      :syntax:

** Headings and Structure

Headings are created with asterisks. The number of asterisks determines the heading level:

#+BEGIN_EXAMPLE
* Level 1 Heading
** Level 2 Heading
*** Level 3 Heading
**** Level 4 Heading
***** Level 5 Heading
****** Level 6 Heading
#+END_EXAMPLE

You can add tags to headings using the ~:tag:~ syntax at the end of the line.

** Text Formatting

Org-mode supports rich inline text formatting:

- *Bold text* using ~*asterisks*~
- /Italic text/ using ~/slashes/~
- _Underlined text_ using ~_underscores_~
- +Strikethrough text+ using ~+plus signs+~
- ~Inline code~ using ~tildes~
- =Verbatim text= using ~=equals signs=~

You can combine formatting: */bold and italic/*, *_bold and underlined_*, etc.

** Lists

*** Unordered Lists

Create unordered lists with ~-~, ~+~, or ~*~:

- First item
- Second item
  - Nested item
  - Another nested item
- Third item

*** Ordered Lists

Create ordered lists with numbers followed by ~.~ or ~)~:

1. First step
2. Second step
   1. Sub-step A
   2. Sub-step B
3. Third step

*** Mixed Lists

You can mix ordered and unordered lists:

1. First ordered item
   - Unordered sub-item
   - Another sub-item
2. Second ordered item
   + Different bullet style
   + Works the same way

** Links and Images

*** External Links

Links use double square brackets: ~[[url][description]]~

- [[https://example.com][Visit Example Website]]
- [[https://github.com/yourusername/org2html][View on GitHub]]
- [[mailto:contact@example.com][Send Email]]

If you omit the description, the URL itself is displayed: [[https://example.com]]

*** Images

Images use the same syntax as links, but the parser automatically detects image file extensions:

[[/images/example.png][Example Image Alt Text]]

Supported formats: ~.png~, ~.jpg~, ~.jpeg~, ~.gif~, ~.svg~, ~.webp~

** Code Blocks

Code blocks support syntax highlighting for multiple languages:

#+BEGIN_SRC javascript
// JavaScript example
function greet(name) {
  return `Hello, ${name}!`;
}

console.log(greet('World'));
#+END_SRC

#+BEGIN_SRC python
# Python example
def fibonacci(n):
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2)

print(fibonacci(10))
#+END_SRC

#+BEGIN_SRC typescript
// TypeScript example
interface User {
  id: number;
  name: string;
  email: string;
}

const user: User = {
  id: 1,
  name: 'John Doe',
  email: 'john@example.com'
};
#+END_SRC

** Tables

Org-mode tables are created with pipes ~|~:

| Feature          | Supported | Notes                        |
|------------------+-----------+------------------------------|
| SEO Metadata     | Yes       | Full Open Graph support      |
| Syntax Highlight | Yes       | Via highlight.js plugin      |
| Vue Components   | Yes       | Through shortcodes           |
| Table of Contents| Yes       | Auto-generated via TOC plugin|
| Responsive Design| Yes       | Mobile-first templates       |

** Special Blocks

*** Quotes

#+BEGIN_QUOTE
This is a blockquote. Use it for highlighting important quotes, testimonials, or cited content from other sources.

Blockquotes can span multiple paragraphs and include other formatting like *bold* and /italic/ text.
#+END_QUOTE

*** Examples

#+BEGIN_EXAMPLE
This is an example block.
It preserves formatting and spacing.
  Including indentation.
    And multiple levels.
#+END_EXAMPLE

*** Centered Text

#+BEGIN_CENTER
This text is centered.
Perfect for important announcements or featured content.
#+END_CENTER

*** Verse (Poetry)

#+BEGIN_VERSE
Roses are red,
Violets are blue,
Org-mode is great,
And so are you!
#+END_VERSE

** Drawers

Drawers are collapsible sections that can contain metadata or additional information:

:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: example-drawer
:CREATED: 2025-01-21
:UPDATED: 2025-01-21
:END:

The ~:PROPERTIES:~ drawer is special and used for metadata. Other drawer types are preserved in the output.

:NOTES:
This is a custom drawer for notes.
You can create any drawer name you want.
:END:

** Footnotes

You can add footnotes[fn:1] to your content for additional context[fn:important] or citations[fn:2].

[fn:1] This is the first footnote with additional information.

[fn:important] This is a named footnote. You can use any label you want.

[fn:2] Footnotes are great for references and citations without cluttering the main text.

** Line Breaks

Use double backslashes ~\\~ to force a line break within a paragraph:\\
This text appears on a new line\\
without starting a new paragraph.

* Vue Component Integration                                  :components:

** Shortcodes

Org2html supports Vue component integration through shortcodes. Use the ~{{< component >}}~ syntax:

{{< Alert type="info" title="Information" >}}

{{< Button variant="primary" size="large" >}}

{{< Card title="Example Card" image="/images/card.jpg" >}}

** Component Mapping

To use shortcodes, create a ~components-map.json~ file in your content directory:

#+BEGIN_SRC json
{
  "Alert": "@/components/Alert.vue",
  "Button": "@/components/Button.vue",
  "Card": "@/components/Card.vue"
}
#+END_SRC

The build process will automatically replace shortcodes with Vue component imports.

* Best Practices                                            :guidelines:

** SEO Optimization

1. *Always include core metadata*: ~TITLE~, ~DESCRIPTION~, ~KEYWORDS~
2. *Use descriptive titles*: 50-60 characters for optimal display
3. *Write compelling descriptions*: 150-160 characters for search snippets
4. *Provide Open Graph images*: 1200x630px for best social media display
5. *Set canonical URLs*: Prevent duplicate content penalties
6. *Use semantic heading structure*: Don't skip heading levels
7. *Add alt text to images*: Improves accessibility and SEO

** Content Structure

1. *Start with an introduction*: Explain what the article covers
2. *Use clear headings*: Break content into logical sections
3. *Keep paragraphs short*: 3-4 sentences for better readability
4. *Use lists for scanability*: Bullet points and numbered lists
5. *Include code examples*: When relevant to your content
6. *Add visual elements*: Images, tables, and diagrams
7. *End with a conclusion*: Summarize key points

** Performance

1. *Optimize images*: Use WebP format when possible
2. *Lazy load images*: Improves initial page load time
3. *Minimize metadata*: Only include necessary fields
4. *Use code splitting*: For large Vue components
5. *Enable caching*: Configure proper cache headers
